chunks: Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: “Is there a reward for the one who practices mutʿah?” He said:

“If by that he seeks the Face of Allah, the Exalted, and opposition to those who deny it, he does not speak to her a single word except that Allah, the Exalted, writes for him thereby a good deed. And he does not extend his hand toward her except that Allah writes for him a good deed. Then when he draws near to her, Allah, the Exalted, forgives for him thereby a sin. Then when he performs ghusl, Allah forgives for him according to the amount of water that passes over his hair.”
I said: “By the number of the hairs?” He said: “Yes, by the number of the hairs.”

key_terms.الشَّعْرِ: the hair, used here to indicate abundance
key_terms.ثَوَابٌ: reward from Allah for the act
key_terms.حَسَنَةً: a good deed written in one’s record
key_terms.لِلْمُتَمَتِّعِ: for the one engaging in mutʿah, i.e. temporary marriage
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: the pleasure and sake of Allah alone

ai.seo_question: What reward does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام mention for mutʿah performed sincerely for Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes reward for mutʿah when it is undertaken seeking the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, and in opposition to those who reject its legitimacy. It presents the act in terms of rewarded speech, rewarded action, and forgiveness of sins, culminating in purification through ghusl.
